summary: IANA created the OTN Signal Type subregistry under the GMPLS Signaling Parameters registry in RFC 7139. This standards-track RFC changes its allocation policy to allow registration through Specification Required.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC changes how entries can be added to the GMPLS OTN Signal Type registry. Standards Track documents use Standards Action, while other documents can use Specification Required.

questions: what is the otn signal type registry
what registration policy does rfc 7892 add
subtitle: Allowing specification-based registrations in the GMPLS OTN Signal Type registry.

tldr.problem: The OTN Signal Type subregistry used only Standards Action, although the RFC allows a second registration procedure for non-Standards-Track documents.
tldr.mechanism: The registry uses Standards Action for Standards Track documents and Specification Required for other documents.
tldr.outcome: The policy update changes the OTN Signal Type subregistry defined by RFC 7139.

today: RFC 7892 is a Standards Track document that updates RFC 7139. It changes the registration policy for the GMPLS OTN Signal Type subregistry.

sections.title: The OTN Signal Type Registry
sections.content: IANA maintains the OTN Signal Type subregistry under the GMPLS Signaling Parameters registry. RFC 7139 defined it with Standards Action as its only registration policy. RFC 7892 updates RFC 7139 to allow Specification Required as well.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry lists OTN signal types used with GMPLS signaling. This RFC adds another process for registering values.

sections.title: Registration Procedures
sections.content: The resulting policy is Standards Action for registrations from Standards Track documents and Specification Required for other documents. The RFC identifies these as the registration procedures for the OTN Signal Type subregistry.
sections.plainLanguage: A Standards Track document must use Standards Action. Other documents may register a value through Specification Required.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says it introduces no new security considerations for existing GMPLS signaling protocols. It points readers to RFC 7139 for specific measures and RFC 5920 for an overview of GMPLS control-plane vulnerabilities and protections.
sections.plainLanguage: The policy change introduces no new security considerations, according to the RFC.
